__comment: Mega has NO OAuth: sign-in is the account EMAIL + PASSWORD. The customUI app com.palm.app.mega-auth renders a two-field form and calls com.palm.service.mega/login, which runs the us0/us handshake and returns the stored session credentials. Unlike the OAuth connectors (shared com.palm.app.cloud-auth), Mega ships its own auth app. MEGA provides BOTH DOCUMENTS and PHOTO.UPLOAD (photo source + device->cloud upload).
__comment2: com.palm.app.mega-auth MUST be in write/readPermissions: createAccount runs under the customUI auth app's identity and is permission-checked against these lists (accounts/handlers/create.js -> Utils.hasPermission).
__comment3: com.palm.service.mega is in read+writePermissions so the service can readCredentials(accountId) for file ops and writeCredentials back (accounts/handlers/credentials.js checks these lists).

capabilityProviders.__comment: The file-picker app and the QuickOffice reroute consume listFolder/downloadFile/uploadFile. The reroute is account-derived (FileStore routes ANY DOCUMENTS capability implemented by a palm://com.palm.service.* URI via the generic 'modern' path, keyed on account _id), so this needs NO per-provider mxId or QuickOffice change. Locators are opaque Mega node handles; the root sentinel 'root' maps to the Cloud Drive root.

Makes the MEGA account a photo source (and device->cloud upload target). The stock Photos aggregator (com.palm.service.photos) discovers PHOTO.UPLOAD accounts and - via the templateId->serviceName fall-through in its Utils.js (see ../photos-integration/) - calls com.palm.service.mega/listAlbums+listPhotos. One folder is surfaced as one album: 'Camera Uploads' under the Cloud Drive root. NOTE: Mega is end-to-end encrypted, so listPhotos DOWNLOADS+DECRYPTS each image to a local file and returns a file:// src_big (the aggregator's curl cannot decrypt Mega's ciphertext URLs).
